events.what: United States and Israeli forces began major combat operations against Iran, announced by the President under claimed Article II authority [iran-ops-transcript].
events.changed: It moved the country from episodic strikes on Iranian nuclear sites to an interstate war conducted without a congressional authorisation for the use of military force [iran-ops-transcript].

events.what: A Pakistan-mediated ceasefire took effect on 8 April 2026 and was formalised in an interim memorandum of understanding on 17 June [whitehouse-epic-fury-ceasefire].
events.changed: It suspended hostilities for about three months and moved the Strait of Hormuz transit question into a negotiated instrument [whitehouse-epic-fury-ceasefire].

events.what: The President declared the ceasefire over, and the naval blockade of Iranian ports was reimposed [cnbc-iran-ceasefire-over][cnn-iran-war-august2026].
events.changed: It returned the country to active hostilities and to interdiction of commercial shipping: United States Central Command reported 44 commercial vessels redirected, two disabled and two boarded as of early August 2026 [cnn-iran-war-august2026].

en.currentState: The blockade remains in force and the war is unresolved; planned strikes were called off on 1 August 2026 and the negotiating channel has moved to Muscat, where Iran and Oman report talks on a new Strait of Hormuz transit route close to conclusion while Iran attributes the strait's closure to the blockade [cnn-iran-war-august2026].

en.thread: Tariff authority struck down and rebuilt

events.what: The Supreme Court held in Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump that the International Emergency Economic Powers Act does not authorise the President to impose tariffs, and the same day Proclamation 11012 imposed a temporary import surcharge of 10 percent ad valorem on most imports under Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974, effective 24 February for 150 days [scotus-learning-resources][fr-proclamation-11012-section122].
events.changed: It voided the legal basis of most of the tariff wall and replaced country-specific rates with a single flat baseline resting on a balance-of-payments authority that the President cannot extend [scotus-learning-resources][fr-proclamation-11012-section122][crs-lsb11398-tariffs].

events.what: The Section 122 surcharge lapsed at its 150-day statutory limit, and Section 301 duties of 10 percent or 12.5 percent on the products of 60 economies took effect the same moment [fr-proclamation-11012-section122][ustr-301-forced-labor-final-action].
events.changed: It moved the tariff base off time-limited emergency authority onto trade-remedy authority carrying no statutory rate ceiling and no fixed expiry, and tied the rate a partner pays to its enforcement of a forced-labour import prohibition rather than to bilateral bargaining [ustr-301-forced-labor-final-action].

en.currentState: The tariff wall now rests on Section 301 and Section 232 actions rather than on emergency economic powers [ustr-301-forced-labor-final-action][crs-lsb11398-tariffs].

en.thread: Lethal military operations in the Western Hemisphere

events.what: The United States executed its first lethal strike on a vessel the Department of War said was operated by a Venezuelan cartel, and on 13 November 2025 the campaign was named Operation Southern Spear [oss-lead-ig-q3-2026].
events.changed: It established standing lethal military action against non-state targets in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific, notified to Congress under the War Powers Resolution rather than authorised by it, with the mission statement and the list of designated targets classified [oss-lead-ig-q3-2026].

events.what: Nicolás Maduro was taken into United States custody by a military operation in Caracas [maduro-capture-wardept][crs-maduro-capture].
events.changed: It removed a sitting head of state by force and placed the United States inside a Venezuelan political transition [maduro-capture-wardept][crs-maduro-capture].

en.currentState: The strike rate is rising while the force and the spending behind it fall: at least 19 vessels were struck and an estimated 56 people killed or presumed dead in the quarter to 30 June 2026, against 12 vessels and 40 people the previous quarter, on quarterly obligations of $173.9 million against $527.0 million and a reduced naval presence the command attributes to a transition to steady-state operations [oss-lead-ig-q3-2026].

events.what: Executive Order 14333 declared a crime emergency in the District of Columbia and directed measures including federal use of the Metropolitan Police Department alongside a National Guard deployment [eo-14333-dc-crime-emergency].
events.changed: It placed a municipal police force under federal direction under the emergency provision of the District of Columbia Home Rule Act, and preceded the federalised National Guard deployments to other cities, one of which the Supreme Court declined to permit in December 2025 [eo-14333-dc-crime-emergency][scotus-trump-v-illinois-2025].

en.currentState: Federalised deployments in Portland, Los Angeles and Chicago were demobilised on 21 January 2026, and Texas National Guard personnel were released from stand-by on 11 March 2026 [northcom-federal-protection-mission].

events.what: Les forces américaines et israéliennes ont lancé des opérations de combat majeures contre l'Iran, annoncées par le président au titre d'une autorité revendiquée en vertu de l'article II [iran-ops-transcript].
events.changed: Cela a fait passer le pays de frappes ponctuelles sur des sites nucléaires iraniens à une guerre interétatique menée sans autorisation du Congrès pour l'emploi de la force militaire [iran-ops-transcript].

events.what: Un cessez-le-feu médié par le Pakistan est entré en vigueur le 8 avril 2026 et a été formalisé dans un protocole d'entente intérimaire le 17 juin [whitehouse-epic-fury-ceasefire].
events.changed: Cela a suspendu les hostilités pendant environ trois mois et a fait passer la question du transit par le détroit d'Ormuz dans un instrument négocié [whitehouse-epic-fury-ceasefire].

events.what: Le président a déclaré le cessez-le-feu terminé et le blocus naval des ports iraniens a été rétabli [cnbc-iran-ceasefire-over][cnn-iran-war-august2026].
events.changed: Cela a ramené le pays à des hostilités actives et à l'interception de la navigation commerciale : le United States Central Command fait état de 44 navires de commerce détournés, deux mis hors d'état et deux arraisonnés au début d'août 2026 [cnn-iran-war-august2026].

fr.currentState: Le blocus demeure en vigueur et la guerre n'est pas réglée ; des frappes prévues ont été annulées le 1er août 2026 et le canal de négociation s'est déplacé à Mascate, où l'Iran et Oman annoncent des pourparlers proches de leur terme sur une nouvelle route de transit dans le détroit d'Ormuz, tandis que l'Iran attribue la fermeture du détroit au blocus [cnn-iran-war-august2026].

events.what: La Cour suprême a jugé dans Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump que l'International Emergency Economic Powers Act n'autorise pas le président à imposer des droits de douane, et le même jour la Proclamation 11012 a imposé une surtaxe temporaire à l'importation de 10 pour cent ad valorem sur la plupart des importations en vertu de la Section 122 du Trade Act of 1974, en vigueur le 24 février pour 150 jours [scotus-learning-resources][fr-proclamation-11012-section122].
events.changed: Cela a anéanti le fondement juridique de l'essentiel du mur tarifaire et remplacé les taux par pays par un seuil unique et uniforme reposant sur une autorité de balance des paiements que le président ne peut pas prolonger [scotus-learning-resources][fr-proclamation-11012-section122][crs-lsb11398-tariffs].

events.what: La surtaxe de la Section 122 a expiré à sa limite légale de 150 jours, et des droits au titre de la Section 301 de 10 pour cent ou 12,5 pour cent sur les produits de 60 économies sont entrés en vigueur au même instant [fr-proclamation-11012-section122][ustr-301-forced-labor-final-action].
events.changed: Cela a fait passer l'assise tarifaire d'une autorité d'urgence à durée limitée à une autorité de recours commercial sans plafond de taux ni échéance fixe, et a lié le taux payé par un partenaire à son application d'une interdiction d'importer des biens produits par le travail forcé plutôt qu'à une négociation bilatérale [ustr-301-forced-labor-final-action].

fr.currentState: Le mur tarifaire repose désormais sur des mesures prises au titre des Sections 301 et 232 plutôt que sur des pouvoirs économiques d'urgence [ustr-301-forced-labor-final-action][crs-lsb11398-tariffs].

fr.thread: Opérations militaires létales dans l'hémisphère occidental

events.what: Les États-Unis ont exécuté leur première frappe létale contre un navire que le Department of War a dit exploité par un cartel vénézuélien, et le 13 novembre 2025 la campagne a reçu le nom d'Operation Southern Spear [oss-lead-ig-q3-2026].
events.changed: Cela a établi une action militaire létale permanente contre des cibles non étatiques dans les Caraïbes et le Pacifique oriental, notifiée au Congrès au titre de la War Powers Resolution plutôt qu'autorisée par lui, l'énoncé de mission et la liste des cibles désignées demeurant classés [oss-lead-ig-q3-2026].

events.what: Nicolás Maduro a été placé sous la garde des États-Unis par une opération militaire à Caracas [maduro-capture-wardept][crs-maduro-capture].
events.changed: Cela a écarté par la force un chef d'État en exercice et installé les États-Unis à l'intérieur d'une transition politique vénézuélienne [maduro-capture-wardept][crs-maduro-capture].

fr.currentState: Le rythme des frappes augmente tandis que les forces et les dépenses qui les portent diminuent : au moins 19 navires ont été frappés et environ 56 personnes tuées ou présumées telles au trimestre clos le 30 juin 2026, contre 12 navires et 40 personnes au trimestre précédent, sur des engagements trimestriels de 173,9 millions de dollars contre 527,0 millions, avec une présence navale réduite que le commandement attribue à un passage en régime permanent [oss-lead-ig-q3-2026].

fr.thread: Commandement fédéral de la police municipale

events.what: Le décret 14333 a déclaré une urgence criminelle dans le district de Columbia et ordonné des mesures comprenant l'emploi fédéral du Metropolitan Police Department ainsi qu'un déploiement de la Garde nationale [eo-14333-dc-crime-emergency].
events.changed: Cela a placé une police municipale sous direction fédérale au titre de la disposition d'urgence du District of Columbia Home Rule Act, et a précédé les déploiements fédéralisés de la Garde nationale dans d'autres villes, dont l'un que la Cour suprême a refusé d'autoriser en décembre 2025 [eo-14333-dc-crime-emergency][scotus-trump-v-illinois-2025].

fr.currentState: Les déploiements fédéralisés à Portland, Los Angeles et Chicago ont été démobilisés le 21 janvier 2026, et le personnel de la Garde nationale du Texas a été libéré de son état d'alerte le 11 mars 2026 [northcom-federal-protection-mission].

peerCorrections.correction: The field carries 2025 trade balances and partner concentration with no tariff content at all, and so describes an import regime that no longer exists. It must now state that the tariffs built on the International Emergency Economic Powers Act were invalidated on 20 February 2026 [scotus-learning-resources]; that a flat 10 percent surcharge under Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974 applied to most imports from 24 February to 24 July 2026 [fr-proclamation-11012-section122]; and that since 24 July 2026 duties of 10 or 12.5 percent apply to the products of 60 economies under Section 301, alongside Section 232 actions [ustr-301-forced-labor-final-action]. The partner-by-partner figures cited predate all three and should be dated as such.

The field attributes projected 2026 growth to the 2025 reconciliation act and the rebound from the late-2025 funding lapse, citing a Congressional Budget Office projection made before 20 February 2026. An across-the-board import surcharge ran for five months of that year and was replaced by a Section 301 regime; the projection must be dated to its vintage and the tariff variable named, or the attribution reads as complete when it is not.

Neither the revenue raised by the 2026 tariff regimes nor the refund exposure from duties collected under the invalidated International Emergency Economic Powers Act tariffs and the lapsed Section 122 surcharge appears in the field. Both bear on the deficit path it states.

Two corrections. First, the field calls the 43-day lapse "the longest full-government shutdown on record"; the source cited supports the duration and the dates, not the superlative. Either cite a source carrying the historical funding-gap series or state the duration alone. Second, the sentence treats the 2025 reconciliation act as the instrument of the period; a second reconciliation act followed, the Secure America Act, Public Law 119-98 of 10 June 2026 (S. 2), which appropriated multi-year funding for Customs and Border Protection personnel, Immigration and Customs Enforcement, and border technology outside the annual appropriations cycle. That is the clearest announced-versus-implemented case in the file and the field does not hold it.

The same unsupported superlative appears here and needs the same treatment. The field also presents two funding lapses where the record of the period shows a third: the fiscal 2026 lapse of 1 October to 12 November 2025, a further lapse resolved by the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 signed on 3 February 2026 [hr7148-appropriations], and the Homeland Security lapse of 14 February to 30 April 2026. The middle one is implied by the source already cited but never stated. Not verified against a primary on this run date.

The field states nuclear modernisation spending but not that the treaty framework limiting it has ended. New START expired on 5 February 2026 with no successor, leaving deployed strategic forces under no legally binding numerical limit; the Under Secretary for Arms Control and International Security Affairs stated this to the Conference on Disarmament on 6 February 2026 (https://www.state.gov/releases/under-secretary-for-arms-control-and-international-security-affairs/2026/02/statement-to-the-conference-on-disarmament). This is a standing condition, which is why it is corrected here rather than carried as an event.

The field carries the January 2026 withdrawal memorandum and the Paris Agreement exit but stops at the instruction; it should record which withdrawals have since completed, the World Health Organization in particular, and should note the New START expiry alongside them as the arms-control component of the same retreat. Verify each completion against a Department of State primary before writing; this run did not verify the World Health Organization completion.

Structural rather than factual: the Iran paragraph is an event chronology living in a standing-conditions field, and it now duplicates the situation thread. The field should keep the relational content it alone can carry — the mediation channels, the Muscat and Doha venues, the effect on allied relationships — and hand the dated sequence of war, ceasefire and resumption to situation.

The sentence "having federalised units for Los Angeles and Portland earlier in the year" omits the District of Columbia action of 11 August 2025, which was not a National Guard federalisation but federal use of a municipal police force under the Home Rule Act, and which preceded the rest [eo-14333-dc-crime-emergency]. The field's account of the period starts one step too late.

The three-lines-of-control passage is the report's clearest statement of who commands what, and it omits the fourth line the period actually used: federal direction of a municipal police force under the District of Columbia Home Rule Act, which runs through neither Article II, nor removal power, nor Title 10 [eo-14333-dc-crime-emergency].

The field says the majority's principal 2025 enactment moved through reconciliation rather than regular order. A second reconciliation enactment followed on 10 June 2026 (Public Law 119-98), which makes the pattern the field describes a settled practice rather than a single instance. The Senate also adopted S.Res. 526 on 14 May 2026, an internal chamber rule withholding senators' pay during funding lapses, effective only after the November 2026 elections — a standing rule, not an event, and it belongs here if anywhere.

The field carries the 2026 rulings on removal at the Federal Trade Commission and the Federal Reserve and on birthright citizenship. Two further 2026 rulings named in the candidate scan, on the Voting Rights Act (Callais) and on terminations of temporary protected status (Mullin), appear nowhere in the file. Verify both against slip opinions and add them here or in rightsAndChecks; this run did not verify them.

The field gives national warming and a vulnerability index but no hazard exposure for the inhabited territories, which the geography field names. Two super typhoons struck the Northern Mariana Islands in 2026; the second, Bavi, produced an emergency declaration on 3 July and a major disaster declaration on 3 August 2026 covering an incident period of 4 to 12 July, with Rota approved for all categories of public assistance (Federal Emergency Management Agency DR-4931-MP, https://www.fema.gov/disaster/4931).

The field and the report use "Department of Defense" throughout, while the department's own publications now carry Department of War as a secondary title under Executive Order 14347 of 5 September 2025 — including the source newly cited in situation. The report should state the dual naming once rather than leave two names for one body unexplained across fields.
